parsed.same_study_reason: Both lists concern a study valuing farm animal welfare costs through stated willingness-to-pay or willingness-to-accept measures. List A discusses marginal willingness to pay for cultured meat as a proxy for altruistic WTP, and List B mentions MWTP for cruelty-free meat alongside pill-scenario valuations. This points to the same paper, though List A is far less detailed.

pairs.reason: Both question whether a stated-preference measure captures genuine welfare or altruistic preferences rather than other motives. A1 targets the cultured-meat MWTP proxy and its confounds (quality expectations, neophobia, naturalism). B6 targets the construct validity of the pill-scenario valuations and only notes that they fail to correlate with cruelty-free MWTP.

Both raise confounding or construct problems in measuring willingness to pay for animal welfare. A2 is about the lack of any confound-free MWTP method (cultured meat, genetically modified animals, welfare labels). B6 is about pill-scenario responses reflecting moral attitudes or misunderstanding.
